"DEADZONE — 3D ARENA FPS

Create a fully playable 3D first-person arena shooter called DEADZONE.

The game combines the tactical atmosphere of competitive military-style FPS games with the fast-paced arcade action of classic arena shooters.

Create an original game identity. Do not reproduce copyrighted characters, maps, weapon models, sounds, or assets from existing games.

1. VISUAL STYLE

- Fully 3D environment.
- First-person perspective.
- Dark futuristic industrial atmosphere.
- Detailed metallic corridors and combat arenas.
- Cinematic lighting and atmospheric fog.
- Realistic-stylized visual presentation.
- Explosions and visual effects.
- Smooth camera movement.

2. PLAYER CONTROLS

Implement:

- WASD movement.
- Mouse camera control.
- Sprint.
- Jump.
- Shooting.
- Reloading.
- Weapon switching.

For Android:

- Virtual joystick.
- Touch camera controls.
- Dedicated fire, reload, jump, and sprint buttons.

3. COMBAT SYSTEM

Implement several original fictional weapons with different gameplay characteristics:

- Standard energy rifle.
- Rapid-fire pulse weapon.
- Heavy fictional projectile launcher.

Each weapon should have:

- Unique visual design.
- Different firing behavior.
- Ammunition capacity.
- Reload animation.
- Distinct sound effects.

4. ENEMY AI

Create multiple fictional enemy types:

- Basic patrol units.
- Fast-moving arena enemies.
- Heavy armored enemies.

Enemies should have simple, readable game AI:

- Patrol designated areas.
- Detect the player within gameplay-defined ranges.
- React to player presence.
- Move around the arena.
- Engage using fictional projectile attacks.
- Have visible health indicators.

5. GAME MODES

Implement:

Arena Survival

- Survive successive enemy waves.
- Enemies become progressively more challenging.
- Display wave progression and score.

Target Practice

- Practice aiming and movement.
- Spawn stationary and moving targets.
- Track accuracy and score.

6. LEVEL DESIGN

Create one fully playable futuristic industrial arena.

Include:

- Multiple interconnected rooms.
- Open combat spaces.
- Elevated platforms.
- Cover objects.
- Atmospheric lighting.
- Distinct environmental details.

7. HUD AND UI

Display:

- Health.
- Armor.
- Ammunition.
- Current weapon.
- Wave number.
- Score.
- Minimap.

Create a polished futuristic interface.

8. AUDIO AND EFFECTS

Add:

- Original fictional weapon sounds.
- Environmental ambience.
- Footsteps.
- Reload sounds.
- Hit feedback.
- Explosions.
- Background music.

9. TECHNICAL REQUIREMENTS

- Use Three.js or another suitable browser-compatible 3D engine.
- Implement actual 3D gameplay, not a 2D image pretending to be 3D.
- Ensure functional player movement and camera control.
- Implement collision detection.
- Optimize performance for Android.
- Include pause, restart, and settings menus.
- Prioritize a functional prototype over excessive visual complexity.

IMPORTANT: Build one polished, playable arena first. Do not attempt multiplayer networking yet.

Test player movement, camera controls, collision, shooting, enemy behavior, and mobile controls before completing the game.

---
This is a build request. Build a complete, playable game now (or apply the requested change to the existing game). Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and note them briefly when you finish.

Screenshots for your own checks: save small JPEGs (a .jpg path, viewport at most 1280px wide) and read only the latest one; older images are dropped from context. Read a full-size PNG only when fine detail matters.
"

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable browser-based 3D first-person arena shooter called DEADZONE, prioritizing one polished arena and a functional prototype.

## Requirements
- Original dark futuristic industrial setting, first-person movement and combat, three fictional weapons, enemy types and AI, survival and target-practice modes, HUD/minimap, audio/effects, pause/restart, and Android touch controls.
- Use Three.js or another browser-compatible 3D engine; include collision, and test gameplay and mobile controls.
- No multiplayer or copyrighted game assets.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained Three.js game in `index.html` using procedural geometry, synthesized audio, and original UI, weapon, and enemy designs.
- Three.js is loaded from `https://unpkg.com/three@0.160.0/build/three.module.js`.

- Captured `screenshots/deadzone-mobile.jpg`.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Complete game implementation.
- `screenshots/deadzone-mobile.jpg`: Latest mobile gameplay capture.
- `screenshots/deadzone-check.jpg`: Earlier desktop capture, taken before the map canvas CSS fix.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local server is available at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Browser console showed only a favicon 404 and SwiftShader/WebGL performance warnings; no gameplay JavaScript errors observed.

## Objective
- Make the existing DEADZONE browser FPS playable on Android landscape screens while preserving its gameplay systems and fixing reported control and gameplay issues.

## Requirements
- Fit landscape screens, avoid HUD overlap, adapt to Android sizes, and prompt users to rotate in portrait.
- Support simultaneous touch movement and aiming, configurable sensitivity, and pitch clamping.
- Improve arena and enemy visibility while retaining the futuristic atmosphere and reasonable shadows.
- Preserve centered camera-aligned shooting, hit confirmation, gameplay systems, weapons, maps, and enemies.
- Fix reloads after ammunition runs out, brighten the arena, and stop bullets at walls.

## Decisions
- Preserve the self-contained Three.js game and improve its current implementation.
- Keep the player spawn at `z=17` to avoid nearby cover and the perimeter wall.
- Track reload timers per weapon so switching weapons during reload does not lose reload progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added portrait rotation prompt, landscape-oriented mobile HUD/control styling, joystick deadzone, separate touch aim region, persistent horizontal/vertical sensitivity settings, and ADS control.
- Improved lighting and reduced fog and vignette darkness; added smooth ADS camera zoom with reset on game start, pause, and game over.
- Updated initial and reset player positions to `z=17`.
- Changed reload handling to track timers per weapon, reject paused/non-running reloads, and show `NO RESERVE AMMO` when empty.
- Included arena solids in the player-shot raycast and added swept wall collision checks for enemy projectiles.
- Extracted the module script and passed `node --check /tmp/opencode/deadzone-check.mjs`.
- Opened the game in Playwright and confirmed the page loads and renders a canvas; captured an 800×360 landscape screenshot at `/tmp/opencode/deadzone-android-landscape.png`.

### Active
- Validate repeated empty-magazine reload cycles and reloads across weapon switches; the browser attempt did not drain the magazine, so reload behavior remains unverified.
- Check that player shots and enemy projectiles stop at walls and cover.
- Review arena brightness and HUD readability on Android landscape; physical Android testing remains outstanding.

### Blocked
- Physical Android device testing has not been performed.

## Next Move
1. Test repeated empty-magazine reload cycles and reloads across weapon switches with reliable gameplay input.
2. Check that player shots and enemy projectiles stop at walls and cover.
3. Review arena brightness and HUD readability on Android landscape; adjust based on findings.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game, weapons/reload logic, projectile and hitscan collision, lighting, and mobile controls.
- `screenshots/deadzone-check.jpg`: Existing gameplay capture.
- `screenshots/deadzone-mobile.jpg`: Existing mobile capture.
- `/tmp/opencode/deadzone-android-landscape.png`: Recent browser screenshot at 800×360.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files including `index.html` are untracked.
- Playwright loaded `http://localhost:3002`; an attempted new `python3 -m http.server 3002` failed because the port was already in use.
- Browser console showed GPU stall warnings and a `favicon.ico` 404; the game page and canvas loaded.

- Preserve the self-contained Three.js game and improve its current implementation.

## Objective
- Make the existing DEADZONE browser FPS playable on Android landscape screens while preserving gameplay systems and fixing reported control and gameplay issues.

## Requirements
- Fit landscape screens, avoid HUD overlap, adapt to Android sizes, and prompt users to rotate in portrait.
- Support simultaneous touch movement and aiming, configurable sensitivity, and pitch clamping.
- Improve arena and enemy visibility while retaining the futuristic atmosphere and reasonable shadows.
- Preserve centered camera-aligned shooting, hit confirmation, gameplay systems, weapons, maps, and enemies.
- Fix reloads after ammunition runs out, brighten the arena, and stop bullets at walls.

## Decisions
- Preserve the self-contained Three.js game and improve its current implementation.
- Keep the player spawn at `z=17` to avoid nearby cover and the perimeter wall.
- Track reload timers per weapon so switching weapons during reload does not lose reload progress.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added a portrait rotation prompt, landscape-oriented mobile HUD/control styling, joystick deadzone, separate touch aim region, persistent horizontal/vertical sensitivity settings, and ADS control.
- Improved lighting and reduced fog and vignette darkness; added smooth ADS camera zoom with reset on game start, pause, and game over.
- Updated initial and reset player positions to `z=17`.
- Updated reload handling to track timers per weapon, reject paused/non-running reloads, and show `NO RESERVE AMMO` when empty.
- Included arena solids in the player-shot raycast and added swept wall collision checks for enemy projectiles.
- Extracted the module script and passed `node --check /tmp/opencode/deadzone-check.mjs`.

### Active

- Verify player shots and enemy projectiles stop at walls and cover.
- Review arena brightness and HUD readability on Android landscape.

- Physical Android device testing has not been performed.
